title: Investigate HTTP round-trip latency in opponent autopass loop
description:
The opponent autopass loop (`_run_opponent_autopass` in `puppeteer/tests/golden_helpers.py`) makes a separate HTTP round-trip for every game callback (`choose_action(no)` -> Java -> HTTP response -> Python -> next call). In CI golden tests, this causes `pass_priority` calls from player A to block for 60+ seconds while waiting for the opponent to process an entire turn's worth of callbacks through the HTTP layer.

This was discovered when `dark_depths_combo` and `initial_decision` golden tests timed out on CI (73-80s replay times exceeding the 60s per-RPC timeout, now bumped to 120s).

Investigation needed:
1. Does the same per-callback HTTP overhead affect real games (not just golden tests)? The real game autopass uses the potato/bridge which may have the same pattern.
2. If so, could the opponent use `pass_priority` exclusively (which handles multiple callbacks in Java without HTTP round-trips) instead of `choose_action` for routine auto-passing? `pass_priority` already auto-handles GAME_SELECT, GAME_PLAY_MANA cancellation, and optional GAME_TARGET cancellation internally.
3. Is the 2-5s per-callback latency specific to GitHub CI runners, or does it also occur on local machines? If CI-specific, the timeout bump to 120s may be sufficient.

Relevant code:
- `puppeteer/tests/golden_helpers.py:525` — `_run_opponent_autopass`
- `Mage.Client.Bridge/src/main/java/mage/client/bridge/BridgeCallbackHandler.java` — `passPriority()` and `chooseAction()`
- `puppeteer/tests/golden_helpers.py:224` — `BridgeSession._rpc` default timeout (bumped from 60s to 120s)
